title: Counters & Rising-Edge Detection
concept:
Machines count things: parts made, cycles run, bottles filled. The trick is the
EDGE — you want to count once per event, not every scan the sensor is TRUE.

A rising-edge "one-shot" uses a memory bit that remembers last scan's value:

    IF Part_Sensor AND NOT Sensor_Prev THEN
        Part_Count := Part_Count + 1;   (* fires once, on the 0->1 edge *)
    END_IF;
    Sensor_Prev := Part_Sensor;         (* remember for next scan *)

Without the edge test, Part_Count would race up every scan the sensor is held
on. The IEC counters (CTU/CTD/CTUD) wrap this pattern in a function block.

Notice the two readings working together: Part_Sensor is used as-is (XIC) while the memory bit is inverted, NOT Sensor_Prev (XIO). A rising edge is simply XIC(input) AND XIO(memory).
ab_note:
Studio 5000 has a one-shot (ONS) and the CTU counter. In ST you often just do
the manual edge shown above with a BOOL memory tag, or call CTU with a
COUNTER/FBD_COUNTER structure: check .DN when .ACC >= .PRE.
task:
Count parts on the RISING edge of Part_Sensor (BOOL). Given the output
Part_Count : DINT and a memory bit Sensor_Prev : BOOL, increment Part_Count by
1 each time Part_Sensor goes from FALSE to TRUE — and only then.

Remember to update Sensor_Prev at the end so the edge is detected next scan.

END_VAR

solution:
(* Lesson 09 -- Counters & Rising-Edge Detection *)
(* Edge = input TRUE now AND memory FALSE last scan  ->  XIC(input) AND XIO(memory). *)

VAR
    Part_Sensor : BOOL;   (* N.O. photo-eye -> XIC (as-is): TRUE while a part is present *)
    Sensor_Prev : BOOL;   (* last scan's sensor state (edge-detect memory)              *)
    Part_Count  : DINT;   (* output: parts counted                                      *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
IF Part_Sensor AND NOT Sensor_Prev THEN
    Part_Count := Part_Count + 1;
END_IF;
Sensor_Prev := Part_Sensor;
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
